rule_friction.idea: Storing the 101x9000 dense tail block of L in float32 to halve the bandwidth of the two GEMVs
rule_friction.rule: must apply the same factorization (data precision) and stay within verify tolerance

rule_friction.idea: Low-rank or compressed form of the tail block (it has full rank 101, so no exact compression exists anyway)
rule_friction.rule: must apply the given factorization, no other operator

rule_friction.idea: Store the dense tail block in float32 (with mixed-precision refinement) to halve the bandwidth of the two dominant sweeps
rule_friction.rule: not an exact application of the given factorization in the fixed float64 type; correctness at the verify tolerance is not guaranteed
rule_friction.expected_gain: about 1.3–1.5x on the tail sweeps (~25% of solve)

rule_friction.idea: Split the tail GEMV/GEMV^T across cores (threads)
rule_friction.rule: target constraints (embedded, single-threaded) and fixed Makefile/build flags (no -pthread/OpenMP)

rule_friction.idea: Compile with -mcpu=native / -ffast-math to get wider unrolling and FMA contraction in the sweeps
